headline: In Portland, every pro comes with a high school attached.
summary: Portland's basketball identity was built in the Portland Interscholastic League. Jefferson, Grant, Benson, Franklin and Wilson (now Ida B. Wells-Barnett) produced Ime Udoka, Terrell Brandon, A.C. Green, the Schimmel sisters and Damon Stoudamire. Rain sets the calendar, and the city now has three pro teams. Nike's opening is Portland-only product that starts in PIL gyms and on Albina courts, and credits the people who built them.

insights.title: Two hometown brands, one backcourt
insights.detail: Nike and Jordan Brand are headquartered in Beaverton, and adidas North America sits on N Greeley Ave in North Portland. Local gyms mix Beaverton samples and early releases with Dame sneakers. In 2026-27 Lillard (adidas) shares the Blazers' backcourt with Ja Morant, who has a Nike signature line. The brand rivalry is now a home-team storyline.
insights.implication: Lead Portland product with Morant and the team, never with Lillard's personal adidas marks. Then compete for the gyms and courts where both companies' families and employees play.

insights.title: The PIL is the pipeline, and locals claim pros by high school
insights.detail: Portlanders tag their pros by school first: Jefferson's Ime Udoka and Terrence Jones, Grant's Terrell Brandon, Benson's A.C. Green, Franklin's Aaron Brooks and Wilson's Damon Stoudamire, who came home to play for the Blazers from 1998 to 2005. Even Domantas Sabonis gets claimed. He was born in Portland in 1996 while his father Arvydas played for the Blazers. Albina's Matt Dishman Community Center and Irving Park are the neighborhood runs.
insights.implication: Make the school the unit of the story. Do school-licensed warm-ups, gym refurbishments and athlete stories that name the high school. Credit the Black Albina coaches and families who built the Jefferson and Grant programs.

insights.title: City versus suburbs is the rivalry that matters
insights.detail: The PIL's inner-city public schools measure themselves against the Catholic powers, Central Catholic and Jesuit, and against suburban 6A programs like West Linn (Payton Pritchard) and Lake Oswego (Kevin Love). Love chose UCLA over his father's alma mater, Oregon, and got heckled at McArthur Court in Eugene.
insights.implication: Keep Portland-city product rooted in the PIL and Albina. Suburban and private-school programs are a different Portland. Blending them into one generic 'Rip City kid' would ring false to both.

insights.title: Women's hoops is the second engine
insights.detail: The WNBA's Portland Fire revived the name of the 2000-02 franchise and finished its first season at Moda Center in 2026. Oregon's Sabrina Ionescu-era teams and the Thorns had already shown how hard the state shows up for women's sports. Franklin High's Shoni Schimmel was MVP of the 2014 WNBA All-Star Game.
insights.implication: Nike makes every WNBA uniform, so the Fire is a second Nike-made home team. Design Rip City product women's-first and keep it selling from May through September, when the Blazers are off.

insights.title: Rain writes the calendar, and summer has a pro-am gap
insights.detail: Portland's wet season runs roughly October to May. Winter pickup moves into community-center gyms like Matt Dishman and under school covered play areas. Outdoor runs at courts like Irving Park peak in the reliably dry July-September window. No Portland summer league has the national weight of Seattle's Crawsover Pro-Am.
insights.implication: Drop outdoor court-wear in July and layered warm-ups in October. Fund a free summer run at Irving Park with Albina organizers. It fills the pro-am gap with something local, not imported.

insights.title: Nike's own stage is already in town
insights.detail: The Nike Hoop Summit has played at Moda Center most Aprils since 2008. The Les Schwab Invitational brings national high school powers to Hillsboro between Christmas and New Year's. The OSAA 6A state finals fill UP's Chiles Center in March. The G League Rip City Remix has played at Chiles in its first seasons.
insights.implication: Make Hoop Summit week the anchor event. It is Nike's event in Nike's home market. Use it for Portland-only drops and PIL youth clinics run by local coaches. Les Schwab in winter and the state finals in spring are the follow-ups.

insights.title: Portland talks hoops through its own outlets
insights.detail: The Blazers left Root Sports in 2024 and built their own over-the-air and streaming setup. Independent coverage runs through SB Nation's Blazer's Edge and Sean Highkin's Rose Garden Report. Its name keeps alive what locals still call the arena, the Rose Garden (renamed Moda Center in 2013).
insights.implication: Seed launches with Portland beat writers and creators before national outlets. 'Rose Garden'-era references, like 1990s and 2000s warm-ups, read as in-group nostalgia to lifelong fans.

places.name: Irving Park courts
places.neighborhood: Irvington / King, inner Northeast (NE 7th Ave and Fremont St)
places.why: Portland's best-known outdoor pickup run, in historically Black Albina, and the natural home for a summer run.

places.name: Matt Dishman Community Center
places.neighborhood: Eliot / King, inner Northeast (NE Knott St)
places.why: A city-run gym that has anchored indoor Albina runs and youth leagues through the wet months.

places.name: Jefferson High School
places.why: Home of the Democrats ('Demos'), the PIL's signature hoops program and Albina's school. It produced Ime Udoka and Terrence Jones.

places.name: Chiles Center, University of Portland
places.why: Home of the Pilots and the G League Rip City Remix, and recent host of the OSAA 6A state finals.

places.name: Moda Center
places.why: Hosts the Blazers, the WNBA's Portland Fire and the Nike Hoop Summit. Locals still call it the Rose Garden.

places.name: Deadstock Coffee
places.why: A sneaker-themed coffee shop founded by former Nike employee Ian Williams, where the city's sneaker and hoops crowd and visiting players turn up. It closed its Old Town storefront in December 2025 and now operates from the lobby café of The Hoxton hotel.

places.name: Liberty High School
places.why: Recent home of the Les Schwab Invitational, Oregon's national-field holiday high school tournament.

places.name: Matthew Knight Arena
places.why: The Ducks' Nike-backed arena, named for Phil Knight's late son, and the statewide pull for Oregon basketball fans.

people.name: Damon Stoudamire
people.role: Wilson High alum, 1996 NBA Rookie of the Year, Blazers guard 1998-2005, college head coach
people.why: 'Mighty Mouse' is the hometown kid who came back to play for the Blazers, and the clearest case of Portland claiming its own.

people.name: Terrell Brandon
people.role: Grant High and Oregon guard, two-time NBA All-Star
people.why: Grant's and Northeast Portland's point-guard standard.

people.name: Ime Udoka
people.role: Jefferson High and Portland State alum, former Blazer, Houston Rockets head coach
people.why: A Jefferson Demo who played for his hometown team and became an NBA head coach: the PIL-to-league path in one career.

people.name: A.C. Green
people.role: Benson Tech and Oregon State forward, three-time NBA champion, the league's 'Iron Man'
people.why: He played an NBA-record 1,192 consecutive games, a Benson-to-Lakers point of PIL pride.

people.name: Shoni and Jude Schimmel
people.role: Umatilla tribal members, Franklin High and Louisville guards; Shoni was 2014 WNBA All-Star Game MVP
people.why: Their move from the Umatilla Reservation to Franklin, told in the documentary 'Off the Rez', made them heroes of Native basketball across the Northwest.

people.name: Payton Pritchard
people.role: West Linn and Oregon guard, Boston Celtics, 2024 NBA champion and 2025 Sixth Man of the Year
people.why: The metro's current NBA standout, and a suburban counterweight to the PIL's claim on the city.

people.name: Portland Fire
people.role: WNBA team, inaugural season 2026 at Moda Center
people.why: A second Nike-uniformed home team that carries Rip City through the summer and anchors women's hoops in the city.

people.name: Rose Garden Report
people.role: Independent Blazers newsletter and podcast by Sean Highkin
people.why: Local-first coverage whose name signals lifelong-fan credibility. A natural place to seed hoops drops.

moments.name: OSAA 6A state basketball finals
moments.why: PIL, Catholic and suburban powers settle the city-vs-suburbs rivalry in front of the whole metro.

moments.name: Nike Hoop Summit
moments.why: Nike's own elite international showcase in Nike's home market. The best week for Portland-only drops and youth clinics.

moments.name: Portland Fire home season
moments.why: Keeps Moda Center and Rip City product in play while the Blazers are off.

moments.name: 1977 championship 50th anniversary
moments.why: Blazermania's 50th. Connect today's PIL and Albina hoopers to the 1977 title the city still measures everything against.

moments.name: Dry-season outdoor runs
moments.why: The only reliable rain-free window. Irving Park and the neighborhood courts fill up, and it is the best time for outdoor product.

moments.name: Rip City Remix G League season
moments.why: An affordable, close-up pro game at the Chiles Center that suits families and youth teams.

moments.name: Les Schwab Invitational
moments.why: Oregon's national-field holiday high school tournament, with peak gifting timing and a crowd of hoop families.

vocabulary.meaning: The Portland Interscholastic League, the city's public-high-school league (said 'P-I-L') and the core of city hoops pride.
Short for the Jefferson High Democrats, Albina's flagship basketball program.
The arena's name from 1995 to 2013. Lifelong fans still use it for the Moda Center as an in-group marker.
The citywide fever around the 1977 title team, now shorthand for peak Blazers fandom.
Damon Stoudamire's nickname, borrowed from the cartoon character and tattooed on his arm. It is the go-to name for any small, fearless Portland guard.
The University of Portland campus on the bluff above the Willamette, home of the Chiles Center.
The fast, pressing, shoot-early style of reservation basketball, which the Schimmels brought to Franklin and Louisville. Use it only with Native partners.
Men's size 9, the standard size for Nike pre-production pairs. Thanks to Beaverton, unreleased samples turn up on Portland courts and in resale shops.

designCues.cue: Wet-asphalt slate: the near-black of an outdoor court after an October drizzle, with painted lines glowing white under park lights
designCues.source: Irving Park and Northeast neighborhood courts through Portland's October-May wet season.
designCues.use: Base color for an outdoor-court capsule, paired with reflective white line graphics. The hex is an approximation, so match it to a lab dip.

designCues.cue: Rip City red as the single saturated hit on slate
designCues.source: The Blazers' red, which has run from the 1977 Blazermania team to every Portland gym and park court.
designCues.use: Use it only on taping, drawcords, a pinwheel-stripe hem or inside plackets, so the slate base reads as Portland weather. Use it under the NBA and Blazers license.

designCues.cue: Ducks green, the color of the state's Nike-backed flagship program
designCues.source: University of Oregon, Phil Knight's alma mater and a long-running Nike uniform test bed.
designCues.use: Use UO marks only under a university license. Without marks, use a fir green as an Oregon-pride accent on statewide pieces.

designCues.cue: Fir line: a continuous row of Douglas-fir silhouettes running along a baseline
designCues.source: Oregon's state tree, and the 'Deep in the Woods' court Tinker Hatfield designed for Matthew Knight Arena in 2011.
designCues.use: Use it as a hem print on shorts or a shooting-shirt yoke. Draw original firs rather than copying UO's court art.

designCues.cue: Claimed by school: a two-tier chest lockup with the high school's name stacked over RIP CITY
designCues.source: Portlanders identify their pros by PIL school first (Jefferson, Grant, Benson, Franklin, Wells).
designCues.use: Use it for PIL team warm-ups and licensed retail versions, set in each school's own varsity lettering and approved by the school.

designCues.cue: Play-shed layer: a hooded shooting shirt with water-repellent shoulders, a mesh back panel and a drop-tail hem
designCues.source: Rain pushes Portland runs under school covered play areas and into drafty community gyms, with a wet walk in and out.
designCues.use: Use it as the uniform for a summer run and as Fire and Blazers warm-ups. Build it in Storm-FIT-type fabric so it works as pregame and street wear.

designCues.cue: Off the Rez: the Schimmel sisters' path from the Umatilla Reservation to Franklin High, Louisville and the WNBA
designCues.source: Shoni and Jude Schimmel and the documentary 'Off the Rez', a defining Northwest Native basketball story.
designCues.use: Use only as a co-authored capsule with the Schimmels and paid, credited artists chosen with the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation. No sacred or ceremonial imagery, and no generic 'tribal' patterns.

productHooks: A Portland-only Ja Morant colorway in wet-asphalt slate (#3B3F45) with Rip City red (#E03A3E), launched with a free run at Matt Dishman. This depends on brand-safety sign-off, on confirming Ja's 2026-27 Nike line and on a Portland door agreeing to carry it.

PIL Pride warm-ups: Nike-made 'claimed by school' shooting shirts for every PIL boys' and girls' varsity team. A school-licensed retail version sends proceeds to Portland Public Schools gym and court repairs.
Rip City Summer Run: a free, Nike-funded July-September run at Irving Park, co-organized and paid with Albina coaches and organizers. Add a court refresh, and the play-shed layer as its uniform.

Hoop Summit week drop: a fir-line shorts and shooting-shirt capsule sold only in Portland that April. Pair it with PIL youth clinics led by local coaches and alumni like Stoudamire and Udoka where available.
A women's-first 'Rip City Hoops' warm-up in a palette shared by the Fire and the Blazers. Launch it at the Fire's 2027 home opener and sell it from May through September.
watchouts: Brand conflict: Damian Lillard is an adidas signature athlete, and adidas North America is headquartered in North Portland. Keep 'Dame Time', 'Dame D.O.L.L.A.' and his signature marks off Nike product. Check whether adidas or Lillard have refurbished any Portland court before Nike touches it.

Vet every athlete partner. Ja Morant served NBA suspensions in 2023 for displaying guns in social videos, and Ime Udoka was suspended by the Celtics in 2022. Do a brand-safety review before any Portland-specific or youth-facing product.

Gentrification along Williams, Mississippi and Alberta has displaced Albina's Black basketball community. Credit and pay Albina coaches, families and organizers, and don't use their courts as a backdrop for outsiders. Keep 'Jail Blazers' and its arrest history off product.
Native hoops: partner with the Schimmels and CTUIR-approved artists, and pay and credit them. Use no sacred or ceremonial imagery, and no Pendleton-style patterns without a license.

Licensing and minors: UO, Oregon State, UP, PPS and PIL school marks, plus OSAA, Les Schwab, Fire and Remix marks, all need licenses. Never feature high school athletes by name or likeness without consent and OSAA compliance.

verify: Confirm Ja Morant's Nike signature-line status for 2026-27 and Nike's brand-safety position on him, and Damian Lillard's current adidas contract, before any Portland signature-shoe or backcourt product.

Find out whether any Portland summer pro-am or streetball league is running now. Find out who organizes the summer runs at Irving Park, and whether adidas, Lillard or the Blazers have refurbished Portland outdoor courts.
Confirm the Nike Hoop Summit 2027 date and venue (Moda Center in recent Aprils), given the pending Moda Center renovation.
Confirm the Portland Fire 2027 schedule, home venue, head coach and uniform palette (Alex Sarama was named coach in 2025).
Confirm the Rip City Remix 2026-27 home venue (Chiles Center in its first seasons) and schedule.
Confirm OSAA 2027 state basketball tournament venues and dates (6A at Chiles Center in recent years), and current PIL membership and classification.
Confirm Les Schwab Invitational December 2026 dates and venue (Liberty High School, Hillsboro in recent years).
Confirm Deadstock Coffee's current location and that the Matt Dishman Community Center gym is open.

Check current roles: Ime Udoka (Rockets head coach), Damon Stoudamire (Georgia Tech head coach as of 2025), Payton Pritchard (Celtics). Check the Schimmel sisters' current public standing and availability before any partnership.
Confirm the Blazers' 2026-27 local TV and streaming setup (own over-the-air network and BlazerVision since leaving Root Sports in 2024), and that Rose Garden Report and Blazer's Edge are active.
Confirm Matthew Knight Arena's current floor design (the 2011 fir-tree court) and University of Oregon colors and licensing terms.
Confirm that Jefferson and Grant remain the PIL's leading basketball programs in 2026-27.
